item.text: {"results":[{"pair_id":"J02325","case1_error":"Divides by four siblings instead of five recipients, omitting Jose from the divisor.","case2_error":"Reports the older brother’s 11 cars as the three-person total, omitting Tommy’s and Jessie’s six cars.","reason":"The first miscounts recipients in equal division; the second answers with one person's count instead of the requested combined total.","judgment":"different"},{"pair_id":"J02326","case1_error":"Reverses the rate calculation, dividing days by words instead of words by days.","case2_error":"Counts weekends as practice days, converts vacation incorrectly, and evaluates 10,000/2888 as 34.72 instead of approximately 3.46.","reason":"The first uses a reciprocal rate relation. The second assigns two boats to space accounting for only one boat and a gap.","judgment":"different"},{"pair_id":"J02328","case1_error":"Doubles the second country's duration to obtain the third's, instead of using the first country's duration for both.","case2_error":"Includes the stationary break in time multiplied by driving speed.","reason":"The first applies a multiplier to the wrong comparison base; the second treats non-driving time as driving time.","judgment":"different"},{"pair_id":"J02329","case1_error":"Uses acquisition cost per egg instead of selling price to calculate sales needed to recover capital.","case2_error":"Uses one student's 105 pens as the pooled total, omitting multiplication by three before subtracting shared usage.","reason":"The first substitutes the wrong monetary rate.
